newsitem.title: FRANCE: UPS deal to boost Air Littoral.
newsitem.headline: UPS deal to boost Air Littoral.

text.p: French airline, Air Littoral, said a one-year, renewable wet-lease agreement signed recently with United Parcel Service Service of America Inc (UPS) was a significant boost to its cargo charter activities.
Earlier this month, UPS launched five weekday feeder flights operated by Air Littoral's two-tonne capacity, cargo-configurated Beechcraft 1900s.

The agreement makes provision for 50 flights per week which will take Air Littoral's annual number of cargo charter flights to around 4,000, Air Littoral's cargo manager, Pierre Fourques, told Reuters.
"The UPS agreement is a big step forward for us but don't intend to stop there, our aim being to gain broad recognition as a charter operator for small, cargo-configured aircraft."
Air Littoral is currently working on the development of other projects in partnership with express distribution companies which could be finalised over the next six months, Fourques said.
One of Air Littoral's five-tonne capacity HS748 aircraft provides charter services on a regular basis for French parcel delivery groups, Calberson and Sernam, between southern France and Corsica.
The HS748 operates a nightly Marseille-Bastia-Ajaccio-Marseille itinerary.
Air Littoral's fleet of ATR42s and Embraer 120120RTs are also available for cargo charter services as they can be from passenger mode, Fourques added.
Air Littoral said it tabled net profits of 8.6 million francs for the financial year ending March 31 1996, from a turnover of 977 million francs.

The Montpellier-based airline is in the process of renewing its fleet with 15 ATR 42-500 passenger aircraft of which six have already been delivered. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
